methodology: Bounded first-pass review of Qur'an 13:6–10, Arabic and English text inspected at Quran.com page 250 and cross-checked against an alternate translation. No pre-Islamic primary source or critical edition independently inspected; possible analogies are research questions only, not verified source relationships. Main, open PR and Supabase ledger union is not yet authoritative; do not treat this branch as merged canonical coverage.

assessments.subject: Demand for immediate punishment, historical exempla, divine forgiveness and severity
assessments.relationship: No source-specific pre-Islamic textual association established
assessments.evidence: Earlier divine-judgment and mercy motifs are plausible comparanda, but no specific passage was critically checked; the verse addresses challengers demanding punishment.

assessments.evidence: Sign-demand and prophetic warning are general narrative motifs; no direct pre-Islamic passage-level relationship established.

assessments.evidence: Possible comparisons to divine knowledge of the unborn require attention to the specific womb-measure language and differing interpretations; no source locator verified.

assessments.evidence: A short theological epithet, not a distinct historical narrative; no exact earlier passage assigned. This is a provisional non-finding, not proof of uniqueness.

historical_dossier.topic: Divine warning, foreknowledge and concealment in Qur'an 13:6–10
historical_dossier.comparative_observation: The passage moves from demands for punitive signs to divine foreknowledge of pregnancy and concealed conduct. Any comparative dossier must distinguish broad shared theological language from demonstrable close textual parallels and attend to the verse-specific claims.
